components: a central descent with a right shoulder
a broad outer bowl returning up the left
strokeOrder: start inside the compact left body and curl round its small inner loop
without lifting, climb its outer left side and curve over into the long top bar
without lifting, carry the long top bar straight to the right
without lifting, come back along the bar to the central upright and start down it
without lifting, descend the central upright to its lower end
without lifting, climb back up the upright and sweep around the broad outer-right curve
without lifting, continue around the bottom bowl toward the far left
without lifting, return up the outer-left side and finish below the top bar — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: one stroke — the manual numbers eight movements: 1–2 the left inner loop, 3 the top bar, 4–5 the shoulder and central descent, and 6–8 the broad outer bowl; native writers draw them without lifting, and this ductus follows them in order, coming back along the bar to the central upright and climbing back up it to reach the outer bowl; cited to Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I, Frame 8, ஞ

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 8, ஞ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 194
strokeOrderSource.variation: Appendix I Frame 8 numbers eight movements: 1–2 build the left inner loop, 3 draws the top bar, 4–5 form the shoulder and central descent, and 6–8 sweep around the broad outer bowl. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows them in order without lifting: the pen starts inside the small loop and spirals out into the top bar, comes back along the bar to the central upright, and climbs back up that upright to where the outer bowl leaves it. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 86% of the 140 stored prototypes of ஞ are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline.

notes: Ña is the palatal nasal heard in combinations such as ஞ்ச. Frame 8's eight numbered movements are one continuous stroke in this font fit: the inner loop, top bar, central descent, and outer bowl follow one another without a lift.
